text: The average age at death of Ukrainian soldiers is 38.8 years.
Russia shifted its force generation from BTGs to divisions and regiments, fixing armies and divisions to axes while rotating battalions.
Because Russian armies and divisions are fixed to axes, Russian commanders stay on familiar ground; Ukraine struggled to match this until the corps reform.
Russian prisoners of war describe their motives for enlisting as mainly financial.
Russian death payments are large enough to change a family's standard of living, while payments for wounds are being cut.
Russia contracted more than 400,000 soldiers in 2024.
HUR counts 403,000 Russian contract recruits in 2025 against a 2026 plan of 409,000.
Budget-derived counts show Russian recruitment in Q1 2026 at a three-year low of 71,216.
Russian regional sign-up bonuses hit record averages of about 1.5M RUB in 2026.
By Ukrainian estimates, 2026 is the first year in which Russian losses outrun recruitment.
Because losses outrun recruitment, Russia is preparing a mobilization contingency of 300,000 a year, by Ukrainian estimates.
A senior Ukrainian official estimates that Russia needs about 400,000 recruits a year just to stand still.
Among the Russian dead confirmed by name to September 2026, the largest groups are contract soldiers (88,600) and volunteers (80,679), followed by prisoners (26,979) and mobilized men (20,350).
Russian volunteers who die are usually over 30 and mobilized men over 25, while early-war dead were 21–23-year-old regulars.
Russia's penal and expendable troops ran from Wagner convicts (2022–23) to Storm-Z (until August 2023) to Storm-V (no pardon, contract until the end of the war).
Ukrainian troops report drug use among Russian assault troops, retreating Russian soldiers being shot, and threats of being "zeroed".
Engineering is a Russian strength: two engineer companies per brigade, doctrinal belts of defences, heavy mining, and concrete command posts.
Russian formations seed mixed AP and AT minefields systematically, while Ukraine, short of mines, seeds only the axes where it expects attacks.
Russian rocket (Zemledeliye) and artillery remote mining close routes deep behind the line.
Russia ordered over 70,000 UMPK glide-bomb kits for 2025.
Russian glide bombs demolish Ukrainian positions, and "no fortification offers adequate protection".
Russian adaptation is reactive: Russia gets better at the problems in front of it but struggles to anticipate new ones.
Russia's answer to the drone kill zone was cheaper, faster and smaller units: motorcycles, then infiltration.
Russia's dependence on Starlink became a single point of failure in February 2026.
Rubikon is a well-funded Russian drone centre of about 5,000 that interdicts roads such as Izium–Sloviansk and hunts Ukrainian drone crews.
North Korean infantry in 2024–25 learned fast but at heavy cost.
Later North Korean deployments shifted to demining and construction, with 1,000 sappers and 5,000 builders announced in June 2025.
By 2026 the North Korean troops in Russia were artillery and reconnaissance units on regular rotation.
A further 10,000 North Korean troops are reportedly being prepared for Russia.

effect: isolates and starves infiltration groups, which are then cleared
rationale: Operation Vivaldi killed the ATV and motorcycle reinforcement and supply of infiltration groups, leaving them stranded and demoralized before clearing them (ISW, MWI).
Russia responded to Vivaldi by shifting south to infiltrate Mykolaivka toward Sloviansk.

measure: Russian drone and C2 use of Starlink
effect: grounded many Russian drones and blinded headquarters
rationale: From 4 February 2026 Starlink whitelisted terminals; this grounded many Russian drones and blinded headquarters.
Russians tried to re-register terminals through Ukrainian proxies.

measure: single-road ground supply of the Kursk salient
rationale: Russian fiber-optic FPVs cut the one road the Kursk salient depended on.
A Zemledeliye launcher was destroyed by FPVs on the Zaporizhzhia front in July 2026.
Ukraine chose bombardment over assault against the Russians besieged in the Vovchansk aggregate plant.

rationale: Turtle tanks absorb FPVs but are nearly blind and their turrets cannot traverse.

Scatterable mines made night resupply through the breach lanes deadly in 2023.
Rain and fog blinded Ukrainian drones before the Huliaipole infiltration.
After Sievierodonetsk, HIMARS hit Russian logistics, which depended on railways.
Ukraine is netting roads against drones in a 15–30 km kill zone.
